Definition: ornament (abstractly or concretely, literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: Glory and beauty are the pair this word carries. Aaron's holy garments were made for glory and for beauty, the Lord Himself shall be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty to the residue of His people, honour and majesty are before Him, and Esther's king showed the riches of his glorious kingdom for a hundred and eighty days.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that beauty is not an extra to God's glory but part of it: the garments, the crown, the sanctuary and the kingdom all shine because He does. I believe a faith that has no room for beauty has missed something the Bible keeps showing — that what belongs to God is glorious, and its glory is beautiful.
